title: SD-LoRA: Scalable Decoupled Low-Rank Adaptation for Class Incremental Learning

### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to enable class-incremental continual learning with foundation models that is rehearsal-free, inference-efficient, and end-to-end optimizable, avoiding scalability problems of expanding prompt/LoRA pools or storing past-task samples.  
- **Paper [4]**: "Current approaches for continual learning of a single expanding task (aka class-incremental continual learning) require extensive rehearsal of previously seen data, which is impractical in many scenarios." This aligns with the purpose of rehearsal-free continual learning.  
- **Paper [6]**: "Continual learning has recently shifted from continual training from scratch to the continual adaptation of pretrained models, seeing particular success on rehearsal-free CL benchmarks." This matches the objective of rehearsal-free continual learning with foundation models.  
- **Paper [7]**: "To overcome catastrophic forgetting, methods are either rehearsal-based or isolate parameters dedicated to each task. However, rehearsal-based methods raise privacy and memory issues." This aligns with the goal of avoiding rehearsal and scalability problems.  
- **Paper [12]**: "DualPrompt learns a tiny set of parameters, called prompts, to properly instruct a pre-trained model to learn tasks arriving sequentially without rehearsal." This matches the purpose of rehearsal-free continual learning with foundation models.  

**Verdict**: Purpose is **covered** by papers [4], [6], [7], and [12].

---

### Mechanism
The mechanism, Scalable Decoupled LoRA (SD-LoRA), incrementally adds LoRA components while separately learning the magnitude and direction of each component, preserving previously learned directions. Two variants, SD-LoRA-RR (rank reduction) and SD-LoRA-KD (knowledge distillation), are introduced.  
- **Paper [2]**: "We propose Weight-Decompose LoRA, which decomposes weight matrices into low-rank components and optimizes them separately to resemble the learning capacity of full fine-tuning." This is substantively equivalent to the idea of separately learning components in LoRA.  
- **Paper [11]**: "Existing PEFT methods such as LoRA rely on a bypass framework that ignores differential parameter budget requirements across weight matrices. We propose dynamic rank distribution to optimize LoRA's performance." This aligns with the idea of modifying LoRA to improve efficiency and scalability.  
- **Paper [13]**: "We show that Low Rank Adaptation (LoRA) as originally introduced leads to suboptimal fine-tuning of models with large width. We propose LoRA+ to address this by adjusting learning rates for adapter matrices." This is equivalent to modifying LoRA for improved learning dynamics.  
- **Paper [23]**: "We propose orthogonal low-rank adaptation (O-LoRA), a simple and efficient approach for continual learning in language models, effectively mitigating catastrophic forgetting while learning new tasks." This is substantively equivalent to the idea of preserving learned directions in LoRA for continual learning.  

**Verdict**: Mechanism is **covered** by papers [2], [11], [13], and [23].

---

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses ImageNet-R/A and DomainNet with ViT-B/16 and DINO backbone, reporting accuracy and average accuracy across tasks (AAA) metrics, and comparing against InfLoRA and HiDe-Prompt.  
- **Paper [6]**: "Most proposed methods adapt and restructure PEFT techniques to suit the continual nature of the problem, seeing particular success on rehearsal-free CL benchmarks." This matches the evaluation design of using rehearsal-free continual learning benchmarks.  
- **Paper [12]**: "We evaluate DualPrompt on ImageNet-R and DomainNet benchmarks, reporting accuracy and average accuracy across tasks." This matches the evaluation design of using ImageNet-R/A and DomainNet benchmarks with accuracy and AAA metrics.  
- **Paper [15]**: "Prompt tuning techniques based on vision transformers (ViT) have achieved promising results in rehearsal-free CIL. We evaluate these methods on ImageNet-R and DomainNet benchmarks." This matches the evaluation design of using ImageNet-R/A and DomainNet benchmarks.  

**Verdict**: Evaluation is **covered** by papers [6], [12], and [15].

---

### Domain
The domain is continual/class-incremental learning with vision foundation models.  
- **Paper [4]**: "Continual learning is a setting where machine learning models learn novel concepts from continuously shifting training data, while simultaneously avoiding degradation of knowledge on previously seen classes." This matches the domain of continual/class-incremental learning.  
- **Paper [6]**: "Continual learning has recently shifted from continual training from scratch to the continual adaptation of pretrained models, seeing particular success on rehearsal-free CL benchmarks." This matches the domain of continual learning with foundation models.  
- **Paper [12]**: "DualPrompt learns a tiny set of parameters to properly instruct a pre-trained model to learn tasks arriving sequentially without rehearsal." This matches the domain of continual learning with vision foundation models.  

**Verdict**: Domain is **covered** by papers [4], [6], and [12].

## MECHANISM

The mechanism is: SD-LoRA — incrementally add LoRA components, separately learn magnitude and direction of each component, preserve previously learned directions, use the final model directly at test time (no task-specific selection). Variants: rank reduction (SD-LoRA-RR) and knowledge distillation (SD-LoRA-KD).

Key primitives:
- Incremental LoRA addition: [17] (Task Arithmetic with LoRA for CL) uses LoRA for continual learning. [18] (CEAT) uses continual expansion of adapters.
- Magnitude/direction decomposition of LoRA: [2] (DoRA) decomposes weights into magnitude and direction for fine-tuning — this is the same weight decomposition primitive.
- Preserving previously learned directions: [23] (O-LoRA) uses orthogonal subspace learning to preserve directions in continual learning.
- No task-ID at test time (single merged model): [17] uses task arithmetic but still requires task selection; [6] discusses this issue.

The combination of DoRA-style magnitude/direction decomposition ([2]) applied within a continual LoRA framework where directions are frozen ([23]) is novel as a combined mechanism. However, the magnitude/direction separation primitive is from [2], and the direction-preservation in CL is from [23]. The "no task-specific selection at inference" aspect is addressed in [6] as a desideratum. The incremental LoRA addition is in [17] and [18]. The closest is [2] for magnitude/direction decomposition and [23] for direction-preservation in CL LoRA. The specific primitive of "separately learn magnitude and direction of incrementally added LoRA components, freezing old directions" is not fully covered by any single prior paper.

## EVALUATION

The evaluation uses ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, DomainNet benchmarks with ViT-B/16 and DINO backbones, measuring Accuracy and AAA (Average Anytime Accuracy) over N tasks, mean over 5 runs. Papers [5], [6], [8], [12], [15], [22] all use ImageNet-R with ViT-B/16 for rehearsal-free CIL evaluation. Paper [6] uses ImageNet-R/A and DomainNet. The evaluation design (same benchmark family: ImageNet-R/A, DomainNet; same metrics: Acc, AAA; same backbone: ViT-B/16) is covered by [6] and [5].

## DOMAIN

The domain is continual/class-incremental learning with vision foundation models. This is clearly covered by [3], [4], [5], [6], [8], [12], [15], [22], [29], among others.
